html:
The Pastos are an Indigenous people of the Andean highlands on the border of southern Colombia and northern Ecuador, in today's Nariño and Carchi provinces. The Colombian city of Pasto, founded by the Spanish in the 1530s, is named after them.

Before the Spanish they lived in farming chiefdoms on the high plateaus, growing potatoes and maize. The Inca Empire pushed into their southern lands in its last decades, around 1500, but its hold was weak. Their own language died out in colonial times, replaced by Spanish, but Pasto communities still keep their communal lands, the resguardos. To their south lived the Otavalo.
